examples.worked_solution:
For a function $f: \mathbb R^n \to \mathbb R,$ given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070131/assets/025dd1a0b89b52e32a3e42e5bd3492261ed060f104f627051b6950c7f94d66c1.png)

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070131/assets/f1a47569220f01e1dc474a13a5040e969449ee0b10cfe7df39c3aec4c6175f41.png)

In our case, we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070131/assets/f0b46d26ccc6fefc404b021bde11c4d6959c00ae0ef1145a9984da602bcc54ef.png)

First, notice that since ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070131/assets/964f8ac9ca9c305faef8562f66d063f318ecbe402df337377bd9efdf61301567.png) 
 we must have

$$
\dfrac{\partial f}{\partial x} = e^y\cos x ,  
\qquad 
\dfrac{\partial f}{\partial y} =e^y\sin x .
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{y}\operatorname{cos}⁡x)=-{e}^{y}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{y}\operatorname{sin}⁡x)={e}^{y}\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{y}\operatorname{cos}⁡x)={e}^{y}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{y}\operatorname{sin}⁡x)={e}^{y}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}-{e}^{y}\operatorname{sin}⁡x & {e}^{y}\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\ {e}^{y}\operatorname{cos}⁡x & {e}^{y}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate this matrix at $(\pi,0).$ This gives

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070131/assets/540c920abd2989b29aae275eedd179c5118e82354915e591c0d1c5296ca9fa21.png)
